doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: Last Chicago gigs and Nevins Wilson
summary: Musically idle in the late sixties, Ware plays last gigs with Vernell Fournier and Willie Pickens and mentions bassist Nevins Wilson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Can you talk a little bit about what you were doing musically in the latter part of the '60s?

Well, I wasn't doing anything around Chicago and my mother died. Musically, it just seemed like there wasn't nothing happening out there with me and I had a bad drinking habit at that time. I kind of got into that A.A. and decided to come back to New York. More musical, you know, more so than Chicago. Chicago was into the organ things, organ groups, with a few clubs out there. Before I left Chicago, though, I worked a little concert with Billy Howell, Campbell (PHONETIC), Wilbur Gamel (PHONETIC) -- let's see, who did we have on piano? I know we had a tenor player, Marvin Cabell (PHONETIC). I forgot the pianist.
No, it wasn't Joe Lee. I don't think it was Joe Lee. It wasn't Willie Pickens (PHONETIC).
No, that was one of the last --

-- last gigs. I had a gig with Vernell Fournier (PHONETIC) out at one of the vocalist clubs. Lurlene Hunter (PHONETIC), young lady been around Chicago for years, good vocalist. She never made what you would call the big time, but she was very well respected. But she had a club. She had

this trio. Vernell the trio in that. Vernell had Willie Pickens on piano, a wonderful Chicago pianist, and he had Nevins Wilson (PHONETIC), my old boy who had [unintelligible] on bass and Nevins had a drinking problem.
Good bass player, but he had it so bad, he spent most of his time in state hospitals.
